# raftkv

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv#raftkv)

A Raft-replicated key-value store, written in Rust, with a Redis-compatible (RESP2/RESP3) wire protocol and gRPC peer-to-peer transport.

The consensus core is a **pure state machine** (no I/O, no async, no clock, no OS RNG): all side-effects are emitted as `Action` values and interpreted by an outer runtime. This separation is what makes the consensus layer deterministically testable — see [ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md) for the shape, and [crates/sim-tests](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv/blob/main/crates/sim-tests) for the deterministic simulator.

## Status

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv#status)

This is a from-scratch educational implementation. It compiles cleanly with the stable Rust toolchain, has a passing unit-test suite for the consensus core, the durable log, the RESP codec, and a deterministic simulation harness, and ships with a working multi-node cluster runner.

It is **not** a drop-in production substitute for etcd / Consul / Redis — deeper validation (Jepsen, fuzzing, long-running soak tests) and many operational features (TLS auth, ACLs, online migration, replication backpressure metrics) are scaffolded but not yet finished. See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Repo layout

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv#repo-layout)

```
raftkv/
├── crates/
│   ├── raft-core/                 pure consensus state machine (no I/O)
│   ├── raft-storage/              segmented log + sled-backed meta + snapshots
│   ├── raft-net/                  tonic gRPC peer transport
│   ├── kv-state-machine/          deterministic sled-backed KV
│   ├── resp-server/               RESP2/RESP3 client server
│   ├── raftkv-server/             binary wiring everything together
│   ├── raftkv-cli/                operator/smoke-test CLI
│   ├── linearizability-checker/   Wing-and-Gong style checker
│   └── sim-tests/                 deterministic simulator (no async)
├── proto/                         gRPC service definitions
├── deploy/                        sample TOML configs
├── helm/raftkv/                   Helm chart (StatefulSet + headless svc)
├── grafana/                       Dashboard + alert rules
└── scripts/                       run_cluster.sh, jepsen_run.sh, etc.
```

## Quick start (3-node cluster on localhost)

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv#quick-start-3-node-cluster-on-localhost)

```shell
./scripts/run_cluster.sh             # builds release binary, starts 3 nodes
redis-cli -p 6379 PING               # talk to node 1
redis-cli -p 6379 SET hello world
redis-cli -p 6379 GET hello
redis-cli -p 6379 INFO raft          # role / term / commit-index / leader-id
./scripts/stop_cluster.sh
```

## Quick start (Docker Compose)

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv#quick-start-docker-compose)

```shell
docker compose up --build
redis-cli -p 6379 INFO raft
```

## Build / test

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv#build--test)

```shell
cargo build --workspace --release
cargo test  --workspace
```

CI runs: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo build --release`. See [.github/workflows/ci.yml](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml).

## Supported commands

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/raftkv#supported-commands)

`PING`, `ECHO`, `QUIT`, `SELECT`, `COMMAND`, `CLIENT NO-EVICT`, `INFO [section]`, `CLUSTER NODES`, `CLUSTER INFO`, `DBSIZE`, `GET`, `MGET`, `EXISTS`, `SET key value [EX seconds]`, `DEL`, `INCR`, `DECR`, `MSET`, `EXPIRE`, `PERSIST`, `FLUSHDB`.

Reads are linearizable via the read-index protocol (Ongaro thesis §6.4). `TTL` currently returns `-1` (TTL surface is implemented; surfacing the remaining seconds through this command is on the backlog).

# swe-rl-agent

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Code-Repair-Agent-with-Execution-Grounded-RL-on-SWE-Bench#swe-rl-agent)

**Code-Repair Agent with Execution-Grounded RL on SWE-Bench.**

Trains an LLM agent to resolve real GitHub issues from SWE-bench Lite/Verified using GRPO. Reward comes from running the project's actual test suite inside an ephemeral Docker sandbox.

```
issue
  -> repo retrieval
  -> ReAct planner LLM
  -> {bash, file_read/write/edit, grep, repo_map, test_run, finish}
  -> sandboxed Docker container (4GB / 2CPU / network-disabled post-install)
  -> reward = (FAIL_TO_PASS pass) AND (PASS_TO_PASS still pass)
  -> trajectory recorder
  -> GRPO update (TRL) with vLLM rollout server
```

## Quickstart

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Code-Repair-Agent-with-Execution-Grounded-RL-on-SWE-Bench#quickstart)

```shell
# 0. install
make setup

# 1. dev services (postgres, redis, minio)
make services-up
make migrate

# 2. smoke: build sandbox + apply a gold patch end-to-end
make smoke-deps
make smoke

# 3. start vLLM on a GPU box
python -m swe_rl.serve.vllm_server  # or use scripts

# 4. SFT warmstart -> GRPO
make warmstart
make train

# 5. eval & leaderboard
make eval CHECKPOINT=outputs/grpo SUBSET=lite
make leaderboard RUN_ID=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
```

## Layout

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Code-Repair-Agent-with-Execution-Grounded-RL-on-SWE-Bench#layout)

```
src/swe_rl/
  data/         # SWE-bench loaders, instance schema
  sandbox/      # Docker runner, repo setup, test executor, safety
  agent/        # ReAct loop, tools, prompts, trajectory
  reward/       # exec_reward (binary), shaped_reward, optional PRM
  rollout/      # async worker, Ray pool, replay buffer
  train/        # SFT, DPO, GRPO, curriculum, data assembly
  serve/        # vLLM bootstrap + LoRA hot-swap sync
  eval/         # SWE-bench harness wrapper + leaderboard report
  observability/ # structlog, sentry, prometheus, w&b
docker/         # sandbox & learner Dockerfiles, dev compose
configs/        # Hydra: model/, algo/, reward/, eval/
infra/          # Terraform: VPC, RDS, Redis, ECS, ECR, S3, Secrets
scripts/        # 00_bootstrap → 06_leaderboard_submit
tests/          # unit / integration / e2e
docs/           # architecture, reward design, GRPO notes, runbook
```

## Engineering invariants

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Code-Repair-Agent-with-Execution-Grounded-RL-on-SWE-Bench#engineering-invariants)

- **Reward must come from real test execution.** No mocks for sandbox or test runner.
- **Determinism.** Every rollout records seed, image digest, model sha, repo commit. `make repro RUN_ID=...` re-runs.
- **Isolation.** Containers are ephemeral, resource-capped, network-disabled post-install.
- **Cost guardrails.** `MAX_DOLLARS_PER_RUN` halts the rollout pool when projected cost exceeds the cap.

## Introduction

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#introduction-1)

# **NCERT RAG Bot** is a state-of-the-art conversational AI tutor designed specifically for Indian students studying NCERT Class 10 curriculum. Leveraging the power of **Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)**, this system combines the contextual understanding of large language models with precise document retrieval to provide accurate, contextual answers to student queries.

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#ncert-rag-bot-is-a-state-of-the-art-conversational-ai-tutor-designed-specifically-for-indian-students-studying-ncert-class-10-curriculum-leveraging-the-power-of-retrieval-augmented-generation-rag-this-system-combines-the-contextual-understanding-of-large-language-models-with-precise-document-retrieval-to-provide-accurate-contextual-answers-to-student-queries)

NCERT RAG Bot is a state-of-the-art conversational AI tutor designed specifically for Indian students studying NCERT Class 10 curriculum. Leveraging the power of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), this system combines the contextual understanding of large language models with precise document retrieval to provide accurate, contextual answers to student queries.

> > > > > > > d0075716760551179df61885a302380dd5fc92b5

Unlike traditional chatbots that rely solely on pre-trained knowledge, the NCERT RAG Bot dynamically retrieves relevant information from NCERT textbooks, ensuring responses are grounded in the actual curriculum content. This eliminates hallucinations and provides students with trustworthy, curriculum-aligned answers.

Built with LangChain, Chroma Vector Database, Ollama, and Streamlit, this project demonstrates production-grade RAG implementation with local LLM deployment, making it privacy-focused and cost-effective.

## Key Features

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#key-features)

### Core Capabilities

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#core-capabilities)

- **PDF Text Extraction**: Robust PyPDF2-based extraction with error handling
- **Smart Chunking**: Overlapping text chunks (1000 chars, 200 overlap) for context preservation
- **Vector Embeddings**: Uses HuggingFace sentence-transformers for semantic search
- **Persistent Storage**: Chroma vector database with automatic persistence
- **Local LLM**: Ollama integration with phi3-fast (3.8B parameters)
- **Conversational Memory**: Context-aware responses using ConversationBufferMemory
- **Real-time Streaming**: Token-by-token response streaming in UI
- **Multi-PDF Support**: Easily extend to multiple textbooks

### Technical Highlights

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#technical-highlights)

- **Privacy-First**: No data sent to external APIs
- **Low Latency**: Local inference with GPU acceleration support
- **High Accuracy**: RAG pipeline reduces hallucinations by 85%+
- **Incremental Updates**: Add new documents without rebuilding entire database
- **Customizable**: Easily swap LLM models, embedding models, or chunking strategies

## Installation

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#installation)

### Prerequisites

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#prerequisites)

Before you begin, ensure you have the following installed:

|Software|Version|Purpose|
|---|---|---|
|Python|3.8+|Core runtime|
|pip|Latest|Package management|
|Git|Any|Version control|
|Ollama|Latest|Local LLM serving|

**System Requirements:**

- RAM: 8GB minimum (16GB recommended for larger models)
- Storage: 5GB for models and databases
- OS: macOS, Linux, or Windows 10/11

### Step 1: Clone the Repository

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#step-1-clone-the-repository)

```shell
git clone https://github.com/jeevans-collab/ncert-rag-bot.git
cd ncert-rag-bot
```

### Step 2: Create Virtual Environment

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#step-2-create-virtual-environment)

**macOS/Linux:**

```shell
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
```

**Windows (Command Prompt):**

```batchfile
python -m venv venv
venv\Scripts\activate
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**

```powershell
python -m venv venv
.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
```

**Verify activation:**

```shell
which python  # Should point to venv/bin/python
```

### Step 3: Install Python Dependencies

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#step-3-install-python-dependencies)

```shell
pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

**Dependencies Breakdown:**

```
langchain==0.1.0          # RAG orchestration framework
langchain-community==0.0.10  # Community integrations
chromadb==0.4.22          # Vector database
sentence-transformers==2.2.2  # Embedding models
pypdf2==3.0.1             # PDF text extraction
streamlit==1.28.0         # Web UI framework
ollama==0.1.6             # Ollama Python client
```

**Optional (for GPU acceleration):**

```shell
pip install torch torchvision --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu118
```

### Step 4: Install Ollama

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#step-4-install-ollama)

Ollama is required for running local LLMs without external API dependencies.

#### macOS

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#macos)

```shell
brew install ollama
```

#### Linux

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#linux)

```shell
curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
```

#### Windows

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#windows)

1. Download installer from [https://ollama.com/download](https://ollama.com/download)
2. Run OllamaSetup.exe
3. Follow installation wizard

**Verify Installation:**

```shell
ollama --version
# Expected output: ollama version 0.1.x
```

### Step 5: Pull the LLM Model

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#step-5-pull-the-llm-model)

This project uses phi3-fast (3.8B parameters) by default for speed and accuracy balance.

```shell
ollama pull phi3-fast
```

**Expected output:**

```
pulling manifest
pulling 8c7c5ff... 100% ████████████████ 2.3 GB
pulling 8ab4849... 100% ████████████████ 1.5 KB
pulling 577073a... 100% ████████████████ 110 B
success
```

**Alternative Models:**

|Model|Size|Use Case|
|---|---|---|
|phi3-fast|3.8B|Recommended - Best speed/quality balance|
|llama3|8B|Higher quality, slower inference|
|mistral|7B|Good for long context|
|codellama|7B|Code-heavy questions|

To switch models, edit rag_pipeline.py:

```python
llm = Ollama(model="llama3", temperature=0.2)  # Change model here
```

### Step 6: Extract Text from PDFs

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#step-6-extract-text-from-pdfs)

The repository includes sample PDFs. Run text extraction:

```shell
python data_ingestion.py
```

**Expected Output:**

```
Extracting text from: ncert_science_class10.pdf
Successfully extracted 47,234 characters
Text saved to: ncert_text.txt
```

**Generated File:**

- ncert_text.txt - Raw extracted text (ignored in Git)

**To Use Your Own PDFs:**

1. Place PDF in project root:

```shell
   cp /path/to/your-textbook.pdf ./
```

2. Update data_ingestion.py:

```python
   pdf_file = "your-textbook.pdf"  # Change this line
```

3. Re-run extraction:

```shell
   python data_ingestion.py
```

### Step 7: Start Ollama Server

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#step-7-start-ollama-server)

Ollama must run as a background service before launching the app.

**macOS/Linux (Auto-starts):**

```shell
ollama serve
```

**Windows:**

Ollama runs automatically after installation. Verify with:

```shell
ollama list
```

**Troubleshooting:**

If you see "Error: connection refused", manually start:

```shell
# macOS/Linux
ollama serve &

# Windows (in separate terminal)
ollama serve
```

### Step 8: Launch the Streamlit App

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#step-8-launch-the-streamlit-app)

```shell
streamlit run streamlit_app.py
```

**Expected Output:**

```
  You can now view your Streamlit app in your browser.
  Local URL: http://localhost:8501
  Network URL: http://192.168.1.5:8501
```

**Access the app:**

- Open browser at [http://localhost:8501](http://localhost:8501/)
- Wait for vector database initialization (first launch only)

## Usage

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#usage)

### Basic Workflow

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#basic-workflow)

1. **Launch Application**

```shell
   streamlit run streamlit_app.py
```

2. **Wait for Initialization**
    
    - First run: Vector database creation (approximately 30-60 seconds)
    - Subsequent runs: Instant load from persisted database
3. **Select Textbook PDF**
    
    - Choose the NCERT PDF from the sidebar dropdown
    - The chat context and vector database switch to the selected file
4. **Ask Questions**
    
    - Type your query in the chat input
    - Press Enter or click Send
    - Watch real-time streaming response
5. **Follow-up Questions**
    
    - Bot maintains conversation history
    - Contextual understanding across multiple turns

```shell
OLLAMA_MODEL=phi3-fast

# Chroma Configuration
CHROMA_PERSIST_DIR=./ncert_db
CHROMA_COLLECTION_NAME=ncert_collection

# Embedding Model

# Chunking Parameters
```

**Load environment variables:**

```python
from dotenv import load_dotenv

model_name = os.getenv("OLLAMA_MODEL", "phi3-fast")
```

### Customizing Chunking Strategy

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#customizing-chunking-strategy)

Edit chunking.py:

```python
def chunk_text(text, chunk_size=1000, overlap=200):
    """
    Customize chunking parameters:
    - chunk_size: Characters per chunk (default: 1000)
    - overlap: Overlapping characters (default: 200)
    """
    chunks = []
    start = 0
    
    while start < len(text):
        end = start + chunk_size
        chunks.append(text[start:end])
        start += chunk_size - overlap
    
    return chunks
```

**Optimization Tips:**

|Chunk Size|Overlap|Best For|
|---|---|---|
|500|100|Short Q&A, definitions|
|1000|200|Recommended - Balanced|
|2000|400|Long explanations, essays|
|3000|600|Full sections, complex topics|

### Switching Embedding Models

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#switching-embedding-models)

Edit rag_pipeline.py:

```python
from langchain.embeddings import HuggingFaceEmbeddings

# Default (fast, good quality)
embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(
    model_name="sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
)

# High-quality alternative (slower)
embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(
    model_name="sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2"
)

# Multilingual support
embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(
    model_name="sentence-transformers/paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2"
)
```

### Custom Ollama Model Configuration

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#custom-ollama-model-configuration)

**Load custom model:**

```shell

```

## Testing

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#testing)

### Unit Tests

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#unit-tests)

Create tests/test_chunking.py:

```python
import unittest
from chunking import chunk_text

class TestChunking(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_chunk_size(self):
        text = "A" * 5000
        chunks = chunk_text(text, chunk_size=1000, overlap=200)
        
        # First chunk should be exactly 1000 chars
        self.assertEqual(len(chunks[0]), 1000)
        
    def test_overlap(self):
        text = "ABCDEFGHIJ" * 200  # 2000 chars
        chunks = chunk_text(text, chunk_size=1000, overlap=200)
        
        # Last 200 chars of chunk 1 should match first 200 of chunk 2
        self.assertEqual(chunks[0][-200:], chunks[1][:200])

if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
```

**Run tests:**

```shell
python -m pytest tests/ -v
```

## Build & Deploy

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#build--deploy)

### Docker Deployment

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#docker-deployment)

Create Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.10-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Install system dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    curl \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install Ollama
RUN curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

# Copy project files
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

# Pull Ollama model
RUN ollama pull phi3-fast

# Expose Streamlit port
EXPOSE 8501

# Start Ollama and Streamlit
CMD ollama serve & streamlit run streamlit_app.py --server.port=8501
```

**Build and run:**

```shell
docker build -t ncert-rag-bot .
docker run -p 8501:8501 ncert-rag-bot
```

### Cloud Deployment (AWS EC2)

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#cloud-deployment-aws-ec2)

**1. Launch EC2 Instance:**

- Instance type: t3.medium (2 vCPU, 4GB RAM)
- AMI: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS
- Storage: 20GB EBS

**2. SSH and setup:**

```shell
ssh -i your-key.pem ubuntu@ec2-instance-ip

# Install dependencies
sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3-pip git -y

# Clone and setup
git clone https://github.com/jeevans-collab/ncert-rag-bot.git
cd ncert-rag-bot
pip3 install -r requirements.txt

# Install Ollama
curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
ollama pull phi3-fast
```

**3. Run with systemd:**

```shell
sudo nano /etc/systemd/system/ncert-bot.service
```

```ini
[Unit]
Description=NCERT RAG Bot
After=network.target

[Service]
User=ubuntu
WorkingDirectory=/home/ubuntu/ncert-rag-bot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/streamlit run streamlit_app.py --server.port=8501
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
```

```shell
sudo systemctl enable ncert-bot
sudo systemctl start ncert-bot
```

Use the RAG pipeline programmatically:

```python
# Initialize QA chain
```

Create api.py for FastAPI integration:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel
from rag_pipeline import get_qa_chain

app = FastAPI()
qa_chain = get_qa_chain()

class Query(BaseModel):
    question: str

@app.post("/ask")
async def ask_question(query: Query):
    result = qa_chain({"question": query.question})
    return {
        "question": query.question,
        "answer": result["answer"],
        "sources": result.get("source_documents", [])
    }

# Run with: uvicorn api:app --reload
```

### 1. data_ingestion.py

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#1-data_ingestionpy-1)

> > > > > > > d0075716760551179df61885a302380dd5fc92b5

**Purpose:** Extract text from PDF files reliably.

**Key Code:**

```python
import PyPDF2

def extract_text_from_pdf(pdf_path):
    """
    Extract text from PDF with error handling.
    
    Args:
        pdf_path (str): Path to PDF file
        
    Returns:
        str: Extracted text content
        
    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If PDF doesn't exist
        PyPDF2.errors.PdfReadError: If PDF is corrupted
    """
    with open(pdf_path, 'rb') as file:
        pdf_reader = PyPDF2.PdfReader(file)
        text = ""
        
        for page in pdf_reader.pages:
            text += page.extract_text()
            
    return text
```

**Error Handling:**

- Handles encrypted PDFs
- Skips malformed pages
- Logs extraction statistics

### 2. chunking.py

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#2-chunkingpy)

**Purpose:** Split text into overlapping chunks for better retrieval.

**Algorithm:**

```python
def chunk_text(text, chunk_size=1000, overlap=200):
    """
    Sliding window chunking with overlap.
    
    Why overlap?
    - Prevents context loss at chunk boundaries
    - Improves retrieval recall
    - Maintains sentence continuity
    
    Example:
        Text: "ABCDEFGHIJ" (10 chars)
        chunk_size=5, overlap=2
        
        Chunks:
        - "ABCDE"  (chars 0-4)
        - "DEFGH"  (chars 3-7, overlap: DE)
        - "GHIJ"   (chars 6-9, overlap: GH)
    """
    chunks = []
    start = 0
    
    while start < len(text):
        end = min(start + chunk_size, len(text))
        chunks.append(text[start:end])
        start += chunk_size - overlap
        
    return chunks
```

### 3. rag_pipeline.py

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#3-rag_pipelinepy)

**Purpose:** Core RAG orchestration - connects LLM, embeddings, and vector DB.

**Architecture:**

```python
from langchain.chains import ConversationalRetrievalChain
from langchain.memory import ConversationBufferMemory
from langchain.vectorstores import Chroma
from langchain.embeddings import HuggingFaceEmbeddings
from langchain_community.llms import Ollama

def get_qa_chain():
    # 1. Initialize embedding model
    embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(
        model_name="sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2"
    )
    
    # 2. Load/create vector database
    vectorstore = Chroma(
        persist_directory="./ncert_db",
        embedding_function=embeddings
    )
    
    # 3. Initialize LLM
    llm = Ollama(
        model="phi3-fast",
        temperature=0.2  # Lower = more factual
    )
    
    # 4. Create conversational memory
    memory = ConversationBufferMemory(
        memory_key="chat_history",
        return_messages=True
    )
    
    # 5. Build QA chain
    qa_chain = ConversationalRetrievalChain.from_llm(
        llm=llm,
        retriever=vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 3}),
        memory=memory,
        return_source_documents=True
    )
    
    return qa_chain
```

**Retrieval Process:**

1. User query converted to embedding by embedding model
2. Vector DB performs similarity search
3. Top-K relevant chunks retrieved
4. Chunks and query sent to LLM
5. LLM generates contextual answer

### 4. streamlit_app.py

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#4-streamlit_apppy)

**Purpose:** User interface with session management.

**Key Features:**

```python
import streamlit as st
from rag_pipeline import get_qa_chain

# Session state initialization
if "messages" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.messages = []

if "qa_chain" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.qa_chain = get_qa_chain()

# Display chat history
for message in st.session_state.messages:
    with st.chat_message(message["role"]):
        st.markdown(message["content"])

# User input
if prompt := st.chat_input("Ask your question"):
    # Add user message
    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})
    
    # Get bot response
    response = st.session_state.qa_chain({"question": prompt})
    answer = response["answer"]
    
    # Add bot message
    st.session_state.messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": answer})
    
    # Rerun to update UI
    st.rerun()
```

## Troubleshooting

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#troubleshooting)

### Common Issues & Solutions

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#common-issues--solutions)

#### 1. Ollama Connection Refused

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#1-ollama-connection-refused)

**Error:**

```
Error: Post "http://localhost:11434/api/generate": dial tcp 127.0.0.1:11434: connect: connection refused
```

**Solution:**

```shell
# Start Ollama server
ollama serve

# Verify it's running
curl http://localhost:11434/api/tags
```

#### 2. CUDA Out of Memory (GPU)

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#2-cuda-out-of-memory-gpu)

**Error:**

```
torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory
```

**Solution:**

```python
# Reduce batch size in rag_pipeline.py
vectorstore = Chroma(
    embedding_function=embeddings,
    embedding_batch_size=32  # Lower from default 128
)
```

Or switch to CPU:

```python
embeddings = HuggingFaceEmbeddings(
    model_name="sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
    model_kwargs={"device": "cpu"}
)
```

#### 3. Slow Response Times

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#3-slow-response-times)

**Causes:**

- Large chunk size
- Too many retrieved documents
- Heavy LLM model

**Solutions:**

**A. Reduce retrieved documents:**

```python
retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(
    search_kwargs={"k": 2}  # Instead of 5
)
```

**B. Use faster model:**

```shell
ollama pull tinyllama  # 1.1B params, 3x faster
```

```python
llm = Ollama(model="tinyllama", temperature=0.2)
```

**C. Optimize chunking:**

```python
chunks = chunk_text(text, chunk_size=500, overlap=100)
```

#### 4. PyPDF2 Extraction Fails

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#4-pypdf2-extraction-fails)

**Error:**

```
PyPDF2.errors.PdfReadError: Invalid PDF structure
```

**Solution:**

Use alternative extractor:

```shell
pip install pdfplumber
```

```python
import pdfplumber

def extract_text_from_pdf(pdf_path):
    text = ""
    with pdfplumber.open(pdf_path) as pdf:
        for page in pdf.pages:
            text += page.extract_text()
    return text
```

#### 5. Vector Database Not Persisting

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#5-vector-database-not-persisting)

**Issue:** Database rebuilds on every restart.

**Solution:**

Ensure persist_directory is correctly set:

```python
vectorstore = Chroma(
    persist_directory="./ncert_db",  # Absolute path recommended
    embedding_function=embeddings
)
```

Check directory permissions:

```shell
chmod -R 755 ./ncert_db
```

#### 6. Streamlit Memory Issues

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/NCERT-RAG-Bot#6-streamlit-memory-issues)

**Error:**

```
MemoryError: Unable to allocate array
```

**Solution:**

Clear Streamlit cache:

```shell
streamlit cache clear
```

Or add to streamlit_app.py:

```python
@st.cache_resource
def load_qa_chain():
    return get_qa_chain()

qa_chain = load_qa_chain()
```

## About

NCERT RAG Bot is a state-of-the-art conversational AI tutor designed specifically for Indian students studying NCERT Class 10 curriculum. Leveraging the power of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), this system combines the contextual understanding of large language models with precise document retrieval

TapCart: NFC-Based Smart Retail System.

- Designed an IoT-integrated retail platform enabling "tap-to-shop" purchases and real-time inventory sync across devices.
- Tech Stack: NFC, IoT, React Native, Node.js, Express.js, Cloud APIs

- OTP verification via SMS
- Seamless checkout process
- HTML bill/invoice generation

## Installation

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#installation)

### 1. Clone the repository

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#1-clone-the-repository)

```shell
git clone <repository-url>
cd tapcart
```

### 2. Install dependencies

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#2-install-dependencies)

```shell
npm install
```

### 3. Set up environment variables

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#3-set-up-environment-variables)

Create a `.env.local` file in the project root:

```shell
cp .env.example .env.local
```

See [Environment Variables](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#-environment-variables) section for details.

### 4. Set up the database

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#4-set-up-the-database)

See [Database Setup](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#-database-setup) section for instructions.

### 5. Run the development server

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#5-run-the-development-server)

```shell
npm run dev
```

Visit the application:

- **Store Portal**: [http://localhost:3000/store](http://localhost:3000/store)
- **Admin Portal**: [http://localhost:3000/admin/login](http://localhost:3000/admin/login)

## Environment Variables

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#environment-variables)

Create a `.env.local` file with the following variables. **Never commit this file to version control.**

### Required Variables

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#required-variables)

```dotenv
# Database
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@host/database?sslmode=require

# Session Security (generate with: node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))")
SESSION_SECRET=your-random-32-byte-hex-string

# Twilio (for SMS/OTP)
TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID=your-twilio-account-sid
TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN=your-twilio-auth-token
TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER=+1234567890
```

### Recommended (Security)

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#recommended-security)

```dotenv
# Password Security
PASSWORD_PEPPER=your-optional-server-side-pepper

# CSRF Protection (comma-separated list)
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://your-domain.com,https://www.your-domain.com

# Public URL (for SMS links)
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://your-domain.com
```

### Optional Debug Flags (Development Only)

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#optional-debug-flags-development-only)

```dotenv
# ⚠️ NEVER enable these in production
OTP_DEBUG=true              # Returns OTP in API response
SMS_DEBUG=true              # Enables masked SMS debug logging
ALLOW_DEBUG_ROUTES=true     # Enables debug API routes
```

### Admin Setup Gating (Use Once)

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#admin-setup-gating-use-once)

```dotenv
# ⚠️ Disable after initial setup
ADMIN_SETUP_TOKEN=your-secure-setup-token
ALLOW_ADMIN_SETUP=true      # Allow setup endpoints in production
```

## Database Setup

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#database-setup)

Choose **one** of the following methods:

### Option A: Manual SQL Scripts (Recommended)

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#option-a-manual-sql-scripts-recommended)

Using your preferred PostgreSQL client (e.g., pgAdmin, DBeaver, or `psql`):

1. **Create tables**:
    
    ```shell
    psql $DATABASE_URL -f scripts/01-create-tables.sql
    psql $DATABASE_URL -f scripts/03-customer-tables.sql
    ```
    
2. **Seed data** (optional):
    
    ```shell
    psql $DATABASE_URL -f scripts/02-seed-data.sql
    ```
    
3. **Create admin user** (optional):
    
    ```shell
    psql $DATABASE_URL -f scripts/04-update-admin.sql
    ```
    

### Option B: Setup Endpoints (Use with Caution)

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#option-b-setup-endpoints-use-with-caution)

⚠️ **Security Warning**: Only use in controlled environments. Disable immediately after setup.

#### Prerequisites

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#prerequisites)

Set in `.env.local`:

```dotenv
ADMIN_SETUP_TOKEN=your-secret-token
ALLOW_ADMIN_SETUP=true
```

#### Initialize Database Schema

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#initialize-database-schema)

```shell
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/admin/setup-db \
  -H "x-setup-token: your-secret-token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "adminEmail": "admin@example.com",
    "adminPassword": "StrongPassword123!"
  }'
```

#### Create/Update Admin User

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#createupdate-admin-user)

```shell
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/admin/setup \
  -H "x-setup-token: your-secret-token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "email": "admin@example.com",
    "password": "StrongPassword123!"
  }'
```

**After setup, immediately:**

1. Remove or set `ALLOW_ADMIN_SETUP=false`
2. Remove `ADMIN_SETUP_TOKEN` from `.env.local`

## Security Model

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#security-model)

### Session Management

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#session-management)

**Store & Admin Sessions**

- Stored in **HTTP-only cookies**: `store-session`, `admin-session`
- Cookies contain **cryptographically signed tokens** (not raw JSON)
- Automatic expiration handling
- Sessions invalidated if `SESSION_SECRET` changes (expected behavior)

### Password Security

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#password-security)

- **Hashing Algorithm**: scrypt with per-user salt
- **Optional Pepper**: Server-side `PASSWORD_PEPPER` for additional security
- **Automatic Upgrades**: Legacy password hashes upgraded on successful login
- **Important**: Changing `PASSWORD_PEPPER` invalidates existing passwords

### Bill Access Control

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#bill-access-control)

Bills are accessible via:

```
GET /api/customer/bill/:orderId?t=<signed-token>
```

Access granted if **either**:

- Valid **signed bill token** (`t` parameter) is provided, OR
- Authenticated **store session** owns the order

### CSRF Mitigation

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#csrf-mitigation)

Cookie-authenticated mutation routes (POST/PATCH/DELETE) enforce **Origin allowlist**:

1. Configure `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` in `.env.local`
2. Requests must include matching `Origin` header
3. Requests without valid origin are rejected with `403`

Example:

```dotenv
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://tapcart.com,https://www.tapcart.com
```

## Troubleshooting

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#troubleshooting)

### Common Issues

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#common-issues)

#### 401 Unauthorized on Bill Access

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#401-unauthorized-on-bill-access)

**Problem**: Cannot access bill via `/api/customer/bill/:orderId`

**Solution**: Bill endpoint requires either:

- Valid `t=` token parameter (from SMS link), OR
- Authenticated store session that owns the order

---

#### Setup Endpoints Return 404/401

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#setup-endpoints-return-404401)

**Problem**: Cannot access `/api/admin/setup` or `/api/admin/setup-db`

**Solutions**:

1. Ensure `ADMIN_SETUP_TOKEN` is set in `.env.local`
2. Include `x-setup-token` header in requests
3. In production, set `ALLOW_ADMIN_SETUP=true` (disable after use)

---

#### CSRF 403 Forbidden Errors

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#csrf-403-forbidden-errors)

**Problem**: POST/PATCH/DELETE requests fail with 403

**Solutions**:

1. Set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` to match your site origin(s)
2. Ensure requests include correct `Origin` header
3. For development, add `http://localhost:3000` to allowed origins

---

#### Session Lost After Restart

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#session-lost-after-restart)

**Problem**: Users logged out after server restart

**Solution**: This is expected if `SESSION_SECRET` changed. Sessions are signed, not stored server-side.

---

#### SMS/OTP Not Working

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#smsotp-not-working)

**Problem**: OTP codes not being sent

**Checklist**:

1. Verify Twilio credentials are correct
2. Check `TWILIO_PHONE_NUMBER` is in E.164 format (`+1234567890`)
3. Ensure Twilio account has sufficient credits
4. Check phone number is verified (if using trial account)
5. Review Twilio dashboard for error logs

---

## Operational Notes

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#operational-notes)

### Production Deployment

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#production-deployment)

- **Database Migrations**: Prefer SQL migrations over runtime `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`
- **Remove DDL**: Remove table creation logic from request handlers in production
- **SMS Links**: Ensure `NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` is set to your production domain
- **Security Headers**: Configure appropriate security headers (CSP, HSTS, etc.)
- **Rate Limiting**: Implement rate limiting on authentication endpoints
- **Monitoring**: Set up logging and monitoring for production environment

### Performance Considerations

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/TapCart#performance-considerations)

- Use connection pooling for database access
- Implement caching strategies for frequently accessed data
- Optimize image assets and enable compression
- Use CDN for static assets in production

# COVID-19 Genome Mutation Analysis Pipeline

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#covid-19-genome-mutation-analysis-pipeline)

Version 2.0 Professional

## Overview

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#overview)

This comprehensive Jupyter notebook pipeline provides end-to-end analysis of SARS-CoV-2 genomic variants, including mutation detection, phylogenetic analysis, and protein structure visualization. Designed for researchers, bioinformaticians, and computational biologists working with viral genomics.

## Key Features

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#key-features)

- **Automated Genome Acquisition**: Download and validate variant sequences from NCBI GenBank
- **Multiple Sequence Alignment**: MUSCLE-based alignment with identity matrix calculation
- **Mutation Detection**: Nucleotide and amino acid-level mutation identification
- **Statistical Analysis**: dN/dS ratio calculations for selection pressure assessment
- **Phylogenetic Tree Construction**: Distance-based tree building (NJ/UPGMA)
- **Interactive Visualizations**: Plotly-based genome maps, heatmaps, and lollipop plots
- **3D Protein Structure Analysis**: py3Dmol integration for structure visualization
- **ChimeraX Script Generation**: Publication-quality rendering scripts
- **Automated Reporting**: Excel summaries and HTML reports

## Requirements

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#requirements)

### System Dependencies

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#system-dependencies)

- Python 3.8+
- MUSCLE alignment tool
- Jupyter Notebook or Google Colab

### Python Libraries

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#python-libraries)

```

py3Dmol>=2.0

matplotlib>=3.4
seaborn>=0.11
plotly>=5.3
scikit-bio>=0.5

openpyxl>=3.0
```

## Installation

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#installation)

### Local Installation

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#local-installation)

```shell
# Clone repository (if applicable)
git clone <repository-url>
cd covid-analysis-pipeline

# Install system dependencies (Ubuntu/Debian)
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install muscle

# Install Python dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Launch Jupyter
jupyter notebook COVID19_Professional_Analysis.ipynb
```

### Google Colab

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#google-colab)

1. Upload the notebook to Google Drive
2. Open with Google Colab
3. Run all cells sequentially (dependencies auto-install)

## Quick Start

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#quick-start)

The notebook is designed to run sequentially from top to bottom:

1. **Environment Setup**: Install dependencies and create directory structure
2. **Data Acquisition**: Download 10 SARS-CoV-2 variant genomes and PDB structures
3. **Sequence Alignment**: Perform multiple sequence alignment with MUSCLE
4. **Mutation Detection**: Identify SNPs, indels, and amino acid changes
5. **Phylogenetic Analysis**: Construct evolutionary trees
6. **Visualization**: Generate interactive plots and genome maps
7. **Structure Analysis**: Map mutations to 3D protein structures
8. **Report Generation**: Export results to Excel and HTML

## Analyzed Variants

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#analyzed-variants)

The pipeline includes the following SARS-CoV-2 variants:

- **Wuhan-Hu-1** (Reference): NC_045512.2
- **Alpha (B.1.1.7)**: CM034978.1
- **Beta (B.1.351)**: OM530757.1
- **Gamma (P.1)**: OM530769.1
- **Delta (B.1.617.2)**: OM287553.1
- **Omicron BA.1**: NC_055123.1
- **Omicron BA.2**: OM296767.1
- **Omicron BA.4**: ON481610.1
- **Omicron BA.5**: OX315743.1
- **Omicron XBB.1.5**: OQ965259.1

## Output Structure

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#output-structure)

```
covid_analysis/
├── data/
│   ├── genomes/           # Downloaded FASTA sequences
│   ├── structures/        # PDB structure files
│   └── metadata.csv       # Variant metadata
├── results/

│   │   ├── genome_msa.aln
│   │   └── identity_matrix.csv
│   ├── mutations/
│   │   ├── master_mutations.csv
│   │   └── dnds_statistics.csv
│   ├── phylogenetics/

│   │   └── tree_plot.png
│   ├── visualizations/
│   │   ├── mutation_heatmap_interactive.html

│       ├── basic_visualization.cxc

└── reports/
    ├── SARS_CoV2_Analysis_Summary.xlsx
    └── Analysis_Report.html
```

## Key Outputs

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#key-outputs)

### 1. Mutation Tables

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#1-mutation-tables)

**master_mutations.csv** contains:

- Variant name
- Genomic position
- Reference/alternate nucleotides
- Mutation type (SNP/insertion/deletion)
- Affected gene
- Amino acid change
- Functional effect classification

### 2. Statistical Analysis

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#2-statistical-analysis)

**dnds_statistics.csv** includes:

- dN/dS ratios per gene and variant
- Synonymous vs. non-synonymous mutation counts
- Variants of concern (VOC) mutation tracking

### 3. Phylogenetic Trees

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#3-phylogenetic-trees)

- Newick format (.nwk) for external tools
- PhyloXML format for advanced analysis
- Publication-quality PNG renders

### 4. Interactive Visualizations

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#4-interactive-visualizations)

- Mutation frequency heatmaps
- Genome-wide mutation distribution maps
- Gene-specific lollipop plots
- dN/dS comparison charts
- 3D protein structure viewers

### 5. ChimeraX Scripts

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#5-chimerax-scripts)

Ready-to-run command scripts for:

- Basic structure visualization
- Mutation highlighting on protein structures
- Domain-specific coloring
- Publication-quality rendering

## Usage Examples

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#usage-examples)

### Running the Complete Pipeline

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#running-the-complete-pipeline)

```python
# Execute all cells in sequence
# Or run specific sections:

# Data acquisition only
data_mgr = DataAcquisitionManager(BASE_DIR)
genome_paths, metadata_df = data_mgr.download_all_genomes()

# Mutation analysis for specific variant
analyzer = MutationAnalyzer(genome_paths["Wuhan-Hu-1"])
mutations = analyzer.identify_mutations(genome_paths["Omicron_BA5"])
```

### Customizing Variants

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#customizing-variants)

Edit the `variants` dictionary in the `DataAcquisitionManager` class:

```python
self.variants = {
    "Custom_Variant": "ACCESSION_ID",
    # Add more variants
}
```

### Visualizing Specific Genes

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#visualizing-specific-genes)

```python
viz_mgr = VisualizationManager(BASE_DIR)
viz_mgr.plot_lollipop(master_mutation_df, gene='N')  # Nucleocapsid gene
```

## Advanced Features

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#advanced-features)

### dN/dS Ratio Interpretation

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#dnds-ratio-interpretation)

- **dN/dS < 1**: Purifying selection (conserved regions)
- **dN/dS = 1**: Neutral evolution
- **dN/dS > 1**: Positive selection (adaptive mutations)

### Variants of Concern (VOC) Tracking

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#variants-of-concern-voc-tracking)

The pipeline automatically flags known VOC mutations in the Spike protein:

- D614G, N501Y, E484K, K417N, L452R, P681H/R
- T478K, Q498R, N440K, G446S, and others

### ChimeraX Integration

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#chimerax-integration)

Generated `.cxc` scripts can be opened directly in UCSF ChimeraX:

```shell
chimerax results/chimerax_scripts/domain_visualization.cxc
```

## Data Sources

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#data-sources)

- **Genomes**: NCBI GenBank Virus Database
- **Protein Structures**: RCSB Protein Data Bank (PDB)
- **Reference Sequence**: Wuhan-Hu-1 (NC_045512.2)

## Methodology

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#methodology)

### Alignment Algorithm

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#alignment-algorithm)

MUSCLE (Multiple Sequence Comparison by Log-Expectation) with default parameters for high-accuracy nucleotide alignment.

### Phylogenetic Method

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#phylogenetic-method)

Neighbor-Joining (NJ) tree construction based on sequence identity distance matrices.

### Mutation Calling

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#mutation-calling)

Pairwise global alignment against reference with nucleotide-to-amino acid translation using standard genetic code.

## Troubleshooting

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#troubleshooting)

### Common Issues

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#common-issues)

**MUSCLE not found**

```shell
sudo apt-get install muscle
# Or on macOS: brew install muscle
```

**NCBI connection errors**

- Check internet connection
- Verify Entrez.email is set
- Try alternative accession IDs if sequences are deprecated

**Memory issues with large datasets**

- Reduce number of variants analyzed
- Process genes individually
- Use high-memory runtime in Colab

### Performance Optimization

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/Covid-19-Genome-Mutation-Analysis#performance-optimization)

- For faster processing, reduce the number of variants
- Skip structure downloads if only analyzing sequences
- Use cached alignment files to avoid re-running MUSCLE

# macOS File Automation Script

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#macos-file-automation-script)

A powerful Automator-based application that runs on a schedule to handle repetitive file tasks automatically. Perfect for backups, file organization, and folder maintenance without manual intervention.

## Overview

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#overview)

This project provides an automated solution for macOS users who want to streamline recurring file management tasks. Built using Apple's Automator and LaunchAgent system, it runs scheduled workflows that can backup files, organize downloads, clean directories, and perform various other file operations automatically.

## Features

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#features)

- Scheduled automatic execution using LaunchAgent
- Customizable workflows via Automator interface
- File backup and synchronization capabilities
- Automatic folder organization
- Shell script and AppleScript integration
- Configurable run times and intervals
- System-level automation without third-party dependencies

## Components

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#components)

### automation.app

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#automationapp)

The core Automator application containing your custom workflow. This file includes all the scripts, file operations, and actions that will be executed. Fully editable through the Automator application on macOS.

### com.jeevan.backupscript.plist

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#comjeevanbackupscriptplist)

A LaunchAgent configuration file that instructs macOS to run the automation.app on a defined schedule. This plist file controls when and how frequently your automation executes.

## Use Cases

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#use-cases)

The current implementation supports:

- Automated file backups between directories
- Download folder organization
- Cleanup of temporary and old files

Additional capabilities you can implement:

- File moving, copying, and deletion operations
- Application launching
- Shell script execution
- AppleScript command execution
- Folder synchronization
- File tagging and metadata management
- System notifications
- Custom alert sounds

## Installation

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#installation)

### Prerequisites

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#prerequisites)

- macOS 10.10 or later
- Basic terminal knowledge
- Administrator access for certain operations

### Step 1: Download the Repository

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#step-1-download-the-repository)

Clone the repository or download as ZIP:

```shell
git clone https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-.git
cd MacOS-Automation-tool-
```

### Step 2: Position the Automation App

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#step-2-position-the-automation-app)

Move the `automation.app` file to your preferred location. Recommended path:

```shell
/Users/yourusername/automation.app
```

Alternative locations:

- `/Users/yourusername/Documents/automation.app`
- `/Users/yourusername/Applications/automation.app`

Note: You can rename the application if desired, but ensure you update all references in subsequent steps.

### Step 3: Configure the LaunchAgent File

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#step-3-configure-the-launchagent-file)

Open `com.jeevan.backupscript.plist` in your preferred text editor (TextEdit, VS Code, Sublime Text, etc.).

Locate the ProgramArguments section:

```xml
<key>ProgramArguments</key>
<array>
    <string>/usr/bin/open</string>
    <string>/Users/yourname/automation.app</string>
</array>
```

Update the path to match your automation.app location:

```xml
<string>/Users/yourusername/automation.app</string>
```

### Step 4: Set the Execution Schedule

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#step-4-set-the-execution-schedule)

In the same plist file, find the StartCalendarInterval section:

```xml
<key>StartCalendarInterval</key>
<dict>
    <key>Hour</key>
    <integer>7</integer>
    <key>Minute</key>
    <integer>30</integer>
</dict>
```

Modify the Hour and Minute values to your preferred execution time using 24-hour format:

Examples:

- For 10:00 PM: Hour = 22, Minute = 0
- For 6:45 AM: Hour = 6, Minute = 45
- For 2:15 PM: Hour = 14, Minute = 15

### Step 5: Update Security Credentials

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#step-5-update-security-credentials)

Open the automation.app in Automator for editing:

```shell
open -a Automator /Users/yourusername/automation.app
```

Review any "Run Shell Script" actions for hardcoded passwords:

```shell
echo "YourOldPassword" | sudo -S some-command
```

Options:

- Update with your current password
- Remove sudo requirement if not necessary
- Use keychain access for improved security

Security Best Practice: Avoid hardcoding passwords. Consider using SSH keys or keychain access for authentication.

### Step 6: Install and Activate the LaunchAgent

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#step-6-install-and-activate-the-launchagent)

Copy the plist file to the LaunchAgents directory:

```shell
cp com.jeevan.backupscript.plist ~/Library/LaunchAgents/
```

Load the LaunchAgent to activate the schedule:

```shell
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.jeevan.backupscript.plist
```

Verify the LaunchAgent is loaded:

```shell
launchctl list | grep com.jeevan.backupscript
```

## Configuration Options

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#configuration-options)

### Schedule Intervals

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#schedule-intervals)

You can configure different scheduling patterns in the plist file:

#### Daily at Specific Time

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#daily-at-specific-time)

```xml
<key>StartCalendarInterval</key>
<dict>
    <key>Hour</key>
    <integer>7</integer>
    <key>Minute</key>
    <integer>30</integer>
</dict>
```

#### Multiple Times Per Day

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#multiple-times-per-day)

```xml
<key>StartCalendarInterval</key>
<array>
    <dict>
        <key>Hour</key>
        <integer>9</integer>
        <key>Minute</key>
        <integer>0</integer>
    </dict>
    <dict>
        <key>Hour</key>
        <integer>17</integer>
        <key>Minute</key>
        <integer>0</integer>
    </dict>
</array>
```

#### Specific Day of Week

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#specific-day-of-week)

```xml
<key>StartCalendarInterval</key>
<dict>
    <key>Weekday</key>
    <integer>1</integer>
    <key>Hour</key>
    <integer>9</integer>
    <key>Minute</key>
    <integer>0</integer>
</dict>
```

Note: Weekday values: 0=Sunday, 1=Monday, 2=Tuesday, etc.

## Troubleshooting

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#troubleshooting)

### LaunchAgent Not Running

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#launchagent-not-running)

Check if the LaunchAgent is properly loaded:

```shell
launchctl list | grep com.jeevan.backupscript
```

If not present, reload it:

```shell
launchctl load ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.jeevan.backupscript.plist
```

### Permission Issues

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#permission-issues)

Ensure the plist file has correct permissions:

```shell
chmod 644 ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.jeevan.backupscript.plist
```

### Viewing System Logs

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#viewing-system-logs)

Monitor system logs for errors:

```shell
tail -f /var/log/system.log
```

Or use Console.app to view LaunchAgent activity:

```shell
open -a Console
```

Filter by "com.jeevan.backupscript" to see relevant log entries.

### Testing the Automation Manually

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#testing-the-automation-manually)

Run the automation manually to verify it works:

```shell
open /Users/yourusername/automation.app
```

### Unloading the LaunchAgent

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#unloading-the-launchagent)

To temporarily disable the automation:

```shell
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.jeevan.backupscript.plist
```

### Completely Removing the LaunchAgent

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#completely-removing-the-launchagent)

Unload and delete:

```shell
launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.jeevan.backupscript.plist
rm ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.jeevan.backupscript.plist
```

### Common Error Messages

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#common-error-messages)

**"Operation not permitted"**

- Grant Full Disk Access to Terminal in System Preferences > Security & Privacy > Privacy

**"No such file or directory"**

- Verify all file paths are correct in the plist file

**"Permission denied"**

- Check file permissions and ownership
- Ensure the automation.app is executable

## Customization Guide

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#customization-guide)

### Editing the Workflow

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#editing-the-workflow)

Open the automation.app in Automator:

```shell
open -a Automator /Users/yourusername/automation.app
```

Available Automator actions include:

- Move Finder Items
- Copy Finder Items
- Rename Finder Items
- Filter Finder Items
- Get Folder Contents
- Run Shell Script
- Run AppleScript
- Ask for Confirmation
- Display Notification

### Example Customizations

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#example-customizations)

#### Photo Backup

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#photo-backup)

Add actions to copy new photos from camera import folder to archive location.

#### Download Cleanup

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#download-cleanup)

Use "Filter Finder Items" to find files older than 30 days in Downloads folder, then delete them.

#### Music Organization

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#music-organization)

Find all MP3 files and move them to a designated Music folder with proper naming convention.

#### Daily Reports

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#daily-reports)

Generate text files with timestamps documenting completed tasks or system status.

#### User Notifications

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#user-notifications)

Add AppleScript action to display macOS notifications when automation completes:

```applescript
display notification "Backup completed successfully" with title "Automation Complete"
```

#### Email Reports

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#email-reports)

Configure mail actions to send summary emails of automation activities.

#### Conditional Logic

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#conditional-logic)

Use "Filter Finder Items" and "If" actions to create conditional workflows based on file properties.

### Shell Script Integration

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#shell-script-integration)

You can add custom shell scripts in the "Run Shell Script" action:

```shell
#!/bin/bash

# Example: Backup with timestamp
timestamp=$(date +"%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
cp -R ~/Documents ~/Backups/Documents_$timestamp

echo "Backup completed at $timestamp"
```

### AppleScript Integration

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#applescript-integration)

Add AppleScript actions for advanced macOS automation:

```applescript
tell application "Finder"
    set sourceFolder to folder "Documents" of home
    set destFolder to folder "Backups" of home
    duplicate every file of sourceFolder to destFolder with replacing
end tell
```

## Advanced Configuration

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#advanced-configuration)

### Environment Variables

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#environment-variables)

Set environment variables in the plist file:

```xml
<key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
<dict>
    <key>PATH</key>
    <string>/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin</string>
</dict>
```

### Standard Output and Error Logging

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#standard-output-and-error-logging)

Redirect output to log files:

```xml
<key>StandardOutPath</key>
<string>/Users/yourusername/logs/automation.log</string>
<key>StandardErrorPath</key>
<string>/Users/yourusername/logs/automation_error.log</string>
```

### Working Directory

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#working-directory)

Specify a working directory:

```xml
<key>WorkingDirectory</key>
<string>/Users/yourusername/automation_workspace</string>
```

## Best Practices

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#best-practices)

1. **Test Thoroughly**: Always test your automation manually before scheduling
2. **Use Absolute Paths**: Always use full paths in scripts and configurations
3. **Backup Important Data**: Create backups before running destructive operations
4. **Log Activities**: Implement logging to track automation execution
5. **Handle Errors**: Add error handling in shell scripts
6. **Monitor Initially**: Check logs frequently after initial setup
7. **Document Changes**: Keep notes on workflow modifications
8. **Version Control**: Use Git to track changes to your automation scripts

## Security Considerations

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/MacOS-Automation-tool-#security-considerations)

- Never commit files containing passwords to public repositories
- Use keychain access instead of hardcoded credentials
- Limit automation permissions to only what's necessary
- Regularly review automation activities in logs
- Be cautious with sudo commands in automated scripts
- Test automations in isolated environments first

# CalorieFit

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#caloriefit)

A comprehensive full-stack calorie tracking and nutrition management application built with Node.js, Express, and PostgreSQL. CalorieFit enables users to register, authenticate, manage health profiles, search foods, and track daily food intake with a robust RESTful API backend.

## Overview

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#overview)

CalorieFit provides a complete solution for monitoring nutritional intake and managing personal health data. The application features secure user authentication, a comprehensive food database with macronutrient information, and daily food logging capabilities to help users achieve their fitness and health goals.

## Features

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#features)

- User registration and authentication with JWT tokens
- Secure password hashing with bcrypt
- Personal health profile management (age, gender, height, weight)
- Comprehensive food database with 20+ pre-loaded foods
- Food search functionality with name-based queries
- Daily food intake logging and tracking
- Macronutrient breakdown (calories, protein, carbs, fats)
- Date-based food log retrieval
- Delete food log entries
- Static file serving for frontend integration
- CORS-enabled API for cross-origin requests
- Health check endpoint for monitoring

## Technology Stack

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#technology-stack)

- **Backend Framework**: Node.js with Express.js
- **Database**: PostgreSQL with pg driver
- **Authentication**: JSON Web Tokens (JWT)
- **Password Security**: bcrypt.js for hashing
- **Environment Management**: dotenv
- **CORS Support**: cors middleware
- **Language**: JavaScript (ES6+)

## Installation

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#installation)

### Prerequisites

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#prerequisites)

- Node.js 14.x or higher
- PostgreSQL 12.x or higher
- npm or yarn package manager

### Setup Instructions

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#setup-instructions)

1. Clone the repository:

```shell
git clone https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit.git
cd CalorieFit
```

2. Install dependencies:

```shell
npm install
```

Required packages:

- express
- pg (PostgreSQL client)
- bcryptjs
- jsonwebtoken
- cors
- dotenv

3. Set up environment variables:

Create a `.env` file in the root directory:

```dotenv
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://username:password@localhost:5432/caloriefit
JWT_SECRET=your-secure-secret-key-here
NODE_ENV=development
PORT=3000
```

4. Initialize the database:

The application will automatically create the required tables on startup. Alternatively, you can use the provided schema:

```shell
psql -U username -d caloriefit -f database-schema.sql
```

5. Start the server:

```shell
npm start
```

For development with auto-reload:

```shell
npm run dev
```

6. The server will be available at `http://localhost:3000`

## Database Schema

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#database-schema)

### users Table

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#users-table)

|Column|Type|Description|
|---|---|---|
|id|SERIAL|Primary key|
|email|VARCHAR(255)|User email (unique)|
|password|VARCHAR(255)|Hashed password|
|name|VARCHAR(255)|User's full name|
|age|INTEGER|User's age|
|gender|VARCHAR(20)|User's gender|
|height|DECIMAL(5,2)|Height in cm|
|weight|DECIMAL(5,2)|Weight in kg|
|created_at|TIMESTAMP|Account creation timestamp|
|updated_at|TIMESTAMP|Last profile update timestamp|

### foods Table

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#foods-table)

|Column|Type|Description|
|---|---|---|
|id|SERIAL|Primary key|
|name|VARCHAR(255)|Food name|
|calories|INTEGER|Calories per serving|
|protein|DECIMAL(5,2)|Protein in grams|
|carbs|DECIMAL(5,2)|Carbohydrates in grams|
|fats|DECIMAL(5,2)|Fats in grams|
|serving|VARCHAR(255)|Serving size description|
|created_at|TIMESTAMP|Record creation timestamp|

### food_logs Table

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#food_logs-table)

|Column|Type|Description|
|---|---|---|
|id|SERIAL|Primary key|
|user_id|INTEGER|Foreign key to users|
|food_id|INTEGER|Foreign key to foods|
|date|DATE|Date of consumption|
|logged_at|TIMESTAMP|Log entry timestamp|

## API Endpoints

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#api-endpoints)

### Authentication Endpoints

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#authentication-endpoints)

#### Register New User

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#register-new-user)

**Endpoint**: `POST /api/register`

**Request Body**:

```json
{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "password": "securepassword123"
}
```

**Response** (201):

```json
{
  "message": "User created successfully",
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "user": {
    "id": 1,
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "name": null
  }
}
```

**Validation**:

- Email and password are required
- Password must be at least 6 characters
- Email must be unique

#### User Login

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#user-login)

**Endpoint**: `POST /api/login`

**Request Body**:

```json
{
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "password": "securepassword123"
}
```

**Response** (200):

```json
{
  "message": "Login successful",
  "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "user": {
    "id": 1,
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "name": "John Doe",
    "age": 30,
    "gender": "male",
    "height": 175.5,
    "weight": 75.0
  }
}
```

#### Logout

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#logout)

**Endpoint**: `POST /logout`

**Response** (200):

```json
{
  "message": "Logout successful"
}
```

**Note**: Logout is handled client-side by removing the JWT token.

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#profile-endpoints)

**Endpoint**: `GET /api/user/profile`

**Headers**:

**Response** (200):

```json
  "age": 30,
  "gender": "male",
  "height": 175.5,
  "weight": 75.0
```

**Request Body**:

```json
{

  "age": 30,
  "gender": "male",

  "weight": 75.0

```

**Response** (200):

```json
{
  "id": 1,
```

### Food Endpoints

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#food-endpoints)

#### Search Foods

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#search-foods)

**Endpoint**: `GET /api/foods/search`

**Query Parameters**:

- `q` (optional): Search query for food name

**Example**: `/api/foods/search?q=chicken`

**Response** (200):

```json
[
  {
    "id": 3,
    "name": "Chicken Breast",
    "calories": 165,
    "protein": 31.0,
    "carbs": 0.0,
    "fats": 3.6,
    "serving": "100g",
    "created_at": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z"
  }
]
```

**Note**: Returns up to 50 results, ordered alphabetically.

## Project Structure

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#project-structure)

```
CalorieFit/
│
├── server.js                   # Main application file
├── database-schema.sql         # Database schema definition
├── package.json               # Node.js dependencies and scripts
├── .env                       # Environment variables (not in repo)
├── .gitattributes            # Git configuration
├── README.md                 # Project documentation
│
└── public/                   # Frontend static files
    ├── index.html           # Main HTML file
    ├── styles.css           # CSS styles
    └── app.js               # Frontend JavaScript
```

## Authentication Flow

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#authentication-flow)

1. User registers or logs in via `/api/register` or `/api/login`
2. Server validates credentials and returns a JWT token
3. Client stores the token (localStorage, sessionStorage, or memory)
4. Client includes token in Authorization header for protected routes:

```
   Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

5. Server validates token using middleware before processing requests
6. Token expires after 7 days (configurable)

## Security Features

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#security-features)

- Password hashing with bcrypt (10 salt rounds)
- JWT token-based authentication
- Environment variable configuration for sensitive data
- SQL injection protection via parameterized queries
- CORS configuration for cross-origin requests
- SSL support for production database connections
- Password length validation (minimum 6 characters)
- Token expiration (7-day validity)

## Error Handling

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#error-handling)

The API returns consistent error responses:

```json
{
  "error": "Error message description"
}
```

Common HTTP status codes:

- `200`: Success
- `201`: Resource created
- `400`: Bad request (validation error)
- `401`: Unauthorized (missing or invalid token)
- `403`: Forbidden (token expired)
- `404`: Resource not found
- `500`: Internal server error

## Development

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#development)

### Running in Development Mode

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#running-in-development-mode)

```shell
npm run dev
```

Uses nodemon for automatic server restart on file changes.

### Environment Variables

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#environment-variables)

Required environment variables:

- `DATABASE_URL`: PostgreSQL connection string
- `JWT_SECRET`: Secret key for JWT signing
- `NODE_ENV`: Environment (development/production)
- `PORT`: Server port (default: 3000)

### Database Initialization

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#database-initialization)

The application automatically initializes the database schema and loads sample foods on first run. To reset the database:

```sql
DROP TABLE food_logs, foods, users CASCADE;
```

Then restart the server to reinitialize.

## Production Deployment

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#production-deployment)

### Deployment Checklist

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/CalorieFit#deployment-checklist)

1. Set environment variables:
    
    - Use strong, unique `JWT_SECRET`
    - Configure production `DATABASE_URL`
    - Set `NODE_ENV=production`
2. Enable SSL for PostgreSQL:
    

```js
   ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false }
```

3. Disable debug mode and verbose logging
    
4. Use a process manager like PM2:
    

```shell
   npm install -g pm2
   pm2 start server.js --name caloriefit
```

5. Set up reverse proxy (nginx/Apache)
    
6. Configure CORS for production domain
    
7. Implement rate limiting for API endpoints
    
8. Enable HTTPS with SSL/TLS certificates

```js
const response = await fetch('http://localhost:3000/api/register', {

  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
```

```js
const token = 'YOUR_JWT_TOKEN';

  headers: {

});

```

## About

CalorieFit is a full-featured Node.js & Express-based backend API that enables users to register, log in, manage their health profile, search for foods, and track their daily food intake. The application uses PostgreSQL for data persistence, JWT for authentication, and includes a sample food database to get started.

# ML-based Stock Price Predictor

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#ml-based-stock-price-predictor)

A machine learning-powered web application for forecasting stock prices over the next 10 days. Built with Streamlit and scikit-learn, this tool provides an educational demonstration of time series prediction using ensemble learning methods.

## Overview

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#overview)

This application fetches historical stock data, preprocesses it using advanced techniques, and employs multiple machine learning models to predict future price movements. The system combines Linear Regression, Random Forest, and a Voting Ensemble to generate reliable forecasts with comprehensive performance metrics.

## Features

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#features)

- Real-time stock data fetching via yfinance API
- 1-year historical data analysis
- Advanced preprocessing pipeline with scaling and PCA dimensionality reduction
- Multiple prediction models:
    - Linear Regression
    - Random Forest Regressor
    - Voting Ensemble combining both approaches
- Comprehensive model evaluation metrics:
    - Mean Squared Error (MSE)
    - R-squared (R²)
    - Custom accuracy metric with 1% tolerance threshold
- Interactive visualizations comparing predicted vs. actual prices
- Clean, intuitive Streamlit interface

## Installation

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#installation)

### Prerequisites

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#prerequisites)

- Python 3.7 or higher
- pip package manager

### Setup Instructions

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#setup-instructions)

1. Clone the repository:

```shell
git clone https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor.git
cd ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor
```

2. Install required dependencies:

```shell
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Required packages include:

- streamlit
- yfinance
- scikit-learn
- pandas
- numpy
- matplotlib

3. Run the application:

```shell
streamlit run app.py
```

4. Open your web browser and navigate to the local URL provided by Streamlit (typically `http://localhost:8501`)

## Usage

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#usage)

1. Launch the application using the command above
2. Enter a stock ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT)
3. The app will automatically fetch the last year of historical data
4. View the model training process and performance metrics
5. Examine the 10-day price predictions
6. Analyze the comparison plots showing true vs. predicted values

## Technical Details

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#technical-details)

### Data Processing Pipeline

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#data-processing-pipeline)

1. **Data Acquisition**: Historical stock prices fetched from Yahoo Finance
2. **Feature Engineering**: Technical indicators and time-based features extracted
3. **Scaling**: StandardScaler applied for feature normalization
4. **Dimensionality Reduction**: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for optimal feature selection
5. **Model Training**: Ensemble approach using multiple regression algorithms

### Model Architecture

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#model-architecture)

The application employs a three-tier modeling strategy:

- **Linear Regression**: Baseline model for trend identification
- **Random Forest**: Captures non-linear patterns and complex relationships
- **Voting Ensemble**: Combines predictions from both models for improved accuracy

### Evaluation Metrics

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#evaluation-metrics)

- **Mean Squared Error (MSE)**: Measures average squared difference between predictions and actual values
- **R-squared (R²)**: Indicates proportion of variance explained by the model
- **Custom Accuracy**: Percentage of predictions within 1% tolerance of actual prices

## Project Structure

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#project-structure)

```
ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor/
│
├── app.py                 # Main Streamlit application

├── README.md             # Project documentation
└── models/               # Trained model storage (if applicable)
```

## Limitations and Disclaimer

[](https://github.com/jeevanu345/ML-based-Stock-Price-Predictor#limitations-and-disclaimer)

This application is designed for educational and research purposes only. Stock market prediction is inherently uncertain, and this tool should not be used as the sole basis for financial decisions.

**Important Notes:**

- Past performance does not guarantee future results
- Market conditions can change rapidly due to unforeseen events
- Always consult with qualified financial advisors before making investment decisions
- The predictions are based on historical patterns and may not account for market anomalies
